subtitle: Build a machine for a particular job

body: Chromehounds is FromSoftware's Xbox 360 mecha combat game, first released in Japan on 29 June 2006. Custom-built HOUNDs fight over Neroimus, an imagined region near the Black Sea. The player assembles a machine whose parts and role affect how it contributes to a battle. The central idea extends beyond winning a duel: a useful HOUND belongs to a group with different responsibilities. Single-player missions introduce those roles, while the original online campaign placed the machines inside a persistent war whose larger direction depended on the competing players and their squads.

Six Role Types provide different ways to participate, from direct combat to support and command responsibilities. The player learns what a machine should accomplish before deciding which equipment makes that possible. Its speed, weapons and arrangement of parts shape the immediate experience of crossing a battlefield. Team planning then connects those individual designs. A powerful gun is useful only if the HOUND carrying it can reach the right place and work with the rest of the squad. Customisation becomes a practical conversation about what the group still needs.

The offline campaign takes place before the Neroimus War, while online play originally presented the conflict itself. Takuji Yoshida directed the game, Toshifumi Nabeshima produced it and Kota Hoshino composed the music. Sega handled its international release in July 2006. The official online servers closed in January 2010, ending the persistent campaign that had supplied much of its identity. Chromehounds remains an unusual experiment in giving a custom machine a social role, where the garage's decisions become meaningful through cooperation with people whose designs can do something different.

A squad needs more than one kind of strength
A war whose online life was brief
